text.p: Trading company and retailer Ceteco Holding NV said on Thursday it had agreed to buy Total Artefactos in Peru.
Total Artefactos is a retailer of consumer electronics and white goods with 29 outlets and expected 1996 turnover of about 50 million guilders, Ceteco said in a statement.
Ceteco, which is 70 percent owned by trading group Hagemeyer, said it will initially buy 75 percent of the shares in the Peruvian retail chain.
At a later stage this can be increased to 100 percent. The Dutch group said it would finance the deal from its own resources but did not elaborate on the financial details.
"Ceteco expects this new acquisition to contribute to (its) income," the company added.
It will buy Total Artefactos from Interamerica de Comercio, which is a subsidiary of Peru's largest business conglomerate Grupo Romero.
"After the acquisition, Ceteco aims to boost Total Artefactos' growth, mainly by opening new branches," Ceteco said.
Ceteco is mainly active in Latin America where it had 277 outlets at the end of June, compared with 259 at the start of this year. Three years ago it had 102 stores in this area.

Ceteco posted 1995 net profit of 25.1 million guilders on turnover of 482 million. In the first half of 1996 it had net profit of 5.8 million guilders on turnover of 287 million. In August it said it expected 1996 full-year sales and profits to show a growth.
